title: Pilot readiness oscillator & KPI probe
content:
Purpose:
Quick working canvas for a small pilot (10–100 customers) to validate performance, cost, and quality signals before wider rollout. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — short checks, measurable thresholds, and clear escalation. Use this as the single source for pilot readiness decisions for sprint N and the adjacent rollback/runbook slots.

Context and scope:
- Feature: adaptive-batching + prefix caching for hosted text-generation endpoints.
- Pilot cohort: 25 early-adopter customers (internal + 10 external pilot accounts).
- Goal window: 2-week pilot to evaluate latency, per-token cost delta, and end-user quality regressions vs baseline model.

Rollout phases (quick):
- Phase A (internal smoke): 1% traffic, internal accounts only, 2 days hard smoke.
- Phase B (alpha pilot): 5% traffic, invited customers, 3–4 days.
- Phase C (beta pilot): 20% traffic, broader cohort, up to 2 weeks.
- Phase D (gradual ramp): 20% -> 100% by manual cadence if all green.

KPI definitions and acceptance thresholds (probe table):
- P99 latency (inference): target <= 350ms, warn >= 400ms, fail >= 650ms. Owner: Jamal.
- Mean cost-per-1k-tokens: target <= baseline * 0.95, warn >= baseline * 1.05, fail >= baseline * 1.10. Owner: Maya.
- Error rate (5xx or runtime failures): target < 0.1%, warn >= 0.5%, fail >= 1.0%. Owner: SRE oncall.
- Quality drift (prompt evaluation failure rate on eval-suite): target delta <= 1.5% worse than baseline, warn >= 3.0%, fail >= 5.0%. Owner: Rina.
- Customer-visible regressions (support tickets / NPS sentiment): warn if > 3 tickets in 24h from pilot cohort, fail if > 8 tickets in 24h. Owner: Customer Success.

Runbook triggers and immediate actions:
- Trigger: P99 latency >= fail threshold for 10 consecutive minutes. Action: auto-toggle fallback to baseline model (immediate), notify #prod-pilot, open incident, SRE investigate.
- Trigger: cost-per-1k-tokens exceed fail threshold for 6 hours. Action: reduce batch size or reduce pilot traffic to Phase A levels, finance notify, exec sync required.
- Trigger: quality drift exceed warn threshold. Action: pause new traffic increase, run targeted evals on affected prompts, optionally roll back.
- Trigger: error rate fail threshold. Action: immediate rollback, page SRE, create postmortem.

Operational checklist (preflight):
- [ ] Canary route configured and verified (routing policy + headers). Owner: Platform eng.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for latency, cost, error, and eval quality live on Console with 1m refresh. Owner: Observability.
- [ ] Tracing enabled end-to-end, sampling at 100% for pilot traffic. Owner: Console and tracing team.
- [ ] Alerting: PagerDuty runbook mapped to thresholds above. Owner: SRE.
- [ ] Customer Success: pilot mailing list + Slack channel created, CS playbook ready. Owner: CS.
- [ ] Billing guardrails: daily cost cap alerts for pilot cohort. Owner: Finance.
- [ ] Legal/Data: privacy checklist signed for external pilot customers (if any). Owner: Legal ops.
- [ ] Rollback button exists in console and has documented verification steps. Owner: DevOPS.

Roadmap tracker (sprint-level snapshot):
- Story: adaptive-batching engine tuning — status: in_review — owner: Jamal — ETA: 2024-11-08 (PR #1289).
- Story: prefix-KV persistent cache persistence option — status: in_progress — owner: Rina — ETA: 2024-11-15.
- Story: pilot telemetry enrichment (customer ids + session tags) — status: blocked (privacy signoff) — owner: Maya — ETA: 2024-11-12.
- Story: rollout orchestration UI (manual override + audit logs) — status: todo — owner: Platform PM — ETA: 2024-11-22.

Weekly cadence and decision gates:
- Daily morning stand (15m): triage any green->amber signals, owner leads provide 10m update.
- Mid-pilot checkpoint (end of Phase B): review KPIs vs thresholds, decide to proceed to Phase C, pause, or rollback. Decision owners: Product lead (Maya), SRE lead, CS lead.
- Final go/no-go after Phase C: require all KPIs in green OR documented and approved mitigations for amber signals.

Escalation matrix (short):
- First responder: SRE oncall + platform eng.
- If unresolved after 30 minutes or customer impact: Product lead + CTO ping.
- If regression in quality or cost at scale: Leadership briefing and finance hold.

Notes, open questions, and heuristics (working):
- How many prompts do we need in eval-suite to detect meaningful drift? Proposal: 120 prompts stratified by length and prompt type (instruction, completion, chat).
- Should we allow per-customer exceptions? Yes, but require explicit opt-in recorded in pilot roster.
- Heuristic: prefer reduced traffic + longer observation windows to rapid rollbacks unless clear failure signals.

Post-pilot artifacts to produce:
- 1-page decision memo (go/no-go rationale).
- Incident/rollback log with timeline and root cause if any.
- Cost delta report with token-level breakdown and bucketed cost drivers.
- Model quality report: evaluation suite comparison + sample prompts that regressed.

Quick action items (this doc):
- Maya: finalize pilot roster and external consent by 2024-10-07.
- Jamal: finish P99 optimization PR and attach benchmark script by 2024-10-09.
- Rina: unblock privacy signoff (Legal) and add 60 eval prompts by 2024-10-10.
- CS: prepare notification templates and support playbook by 2024-10-11.

Slack channels and key links:
- #pilot-adopting (alerts + ad-hoc discussion)
- #prod-pilot (incidents + telemetry)
- Linear ticket: PD-421 (pilot instrumentation)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289

Quick history of changes (live):
- 2024-10-03: initial draft (Maya).
- 2024-10-09: added runbook triggers + Sprint tracker (Jamal).
- 2024-11-12: updated thresholds after lab benchmarks and alignment with SRE (Rina).

Bottom line: run the pilot slowly, measure rigorously, keep rollback easy and visible. This canvas should be the lightweight single source for the pilot decision at the end of sprint N.
